definitions.explanation: Water flowing with great speed and force, as in a flooded river or a mountain stream in spring.
An overwhelming flow of something that sweeps people along: history, emotions, information.

examples.japanese: ⟦{川|かわ}→川：02186_kawa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{奔流|ほんりゅう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The river turned into a torrent.

examples.japanese: ⟦{雪解|ゆきど}け→雪解け：08558_yukidoke⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{奔流|ほんりゅう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{谷|たに}→谷：02223_tani⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|くだ}る→下る：03913_kudaru⟧。
examples.english: Snowmelt rushes down the valley in a torrent.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大雨|おおあめ}→大雨：03015_ooame⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧、⟦{穏|おだ}やか→穏やか：02353_odayaka⟧だった⟦{小川|おがわ}→小川：06695_ogawa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{茶色|ちゃいろ}い→茶色い：00922_chairoi⟧{奔流|ほんりゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{変|か}わっていた→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: After the heavy rain, the gentle stream had become a brown torrent.

examples.english: Many people were swept up in the tide of the times and left their hometowns.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary word, at home in novels, essays and serious journalism. In ordinary talk about rivers, people say ⟦{激流|げきりゅう}→激流：13432_gekiryuu⟧ or ⟦{急流|きゅうりゅう}→急流：16388_kyuuryuu⟧, or simply ⟦{流|なが}れ→流れ：03504_nagare⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{速|はや}い→速い：00514_hayai⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {奔流|ほんりゅう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become a torrent
- ⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{奔流|ほんりゅう}: the tide of the times
- ⟦{感情|かんじょう}→感情：00171_kanjou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{奔流|ほんりゅう}: a rush of emotion

WATCH OUT:
⟦{本流|ほんりゅう}→本流：25798_honryuu⟧ (the main stream of a river; the mainstream) has the same reading but means the central current, not a violent one.
